Tables 21-22. First-line (amitriptyline, fluoxetine, sertraline) and second-line (duloxetine) antidepressants for major depressive disorder: doses, titration, maximum doses
MedicineDoseFrequencyDurationMax doseCodes
Table 21 - First line: tricyclic antidepressants
Amitriptyline poInitial dose 25 mg for 3 days, then 50 mgBedtimeShort to long-term150-200 mg/dayA E
Then increase the dose gradually by 25 mg at an interval of 7-14 days if there is no response.
Table 21 - First line: SSRIs (alternative)
Fluoxetine poInitial dose 10-20 mgOnce dailyShort to long-term60-80 mg/dayA E
Increase the dose gradually by 10-20 mg at an interval of 4-8 weeks if there is no response.
Sertraline poInitial dose 25-50 mgBedtimeShort to long-term200 mg/dayA E
Increase the dose gradually by 25-50 mg at an interval of 7-14 days if there is no response.
Table 22 - Second line: SNRI
Duloxetine poInitial dose 20-30 mgOnce dailyShort to long-term120 mg/dayS E
Increase the dose gradually by 20-30 mg at an interval of 7-14 days if there is no response.
Amitriptyline is better prescribed if sedation is desirable. Fluoxetine and sertraline are better if sedation is not desirable, and for depression with suicidality, the elderly, children and frail physically ill patients.

Points to check in the source:
  • Risperidone titration is printed 'by 50-200mg' (Table 24); risperidone is titrated in 0.5-1 mg steps (max 6 mg/day). The 50-200 mg figure appears copied from sulpiride/chlorpromazine.
  • Olanzapine maximum is given as 25 mg/day here and in Table 31; the usual maximum is 20 mg/day.

Tables 23-24. Major depressive disorder: lorazepam for insomnia; antipsychotics (haloperidol, risperidone, olanzapine, aripiprazole) for depression with psychosis – doses and titration; cautions for SSRIs and TCAs
MedicineDoseFrequencyDurationMax doseCodes
Table 23 - Insomnia in major depressive disorder
Lorazepam po1-2 mgBedtime5-7 days2 mgB E
Table 24 - Depressive disorder with psychosis: prescribe antidepressants concurrently with one antipsychotic
Haloperidol poInitial dose 1.5-3 mgOnce to twice a dayShort to long-term20 mg/dayA E
Increase the dose gradually by 1.5 mg at an interval of 7-14 days if the patient presents with psychosis.
Risperidone poInitial dose 1-2 mgOnce to twice a dayShort to long-term6 mg/dayB E
Increase the dose gradually at an interval of 3-14 days by 50-200mg [as printed] if the patient presents with psychosis.
Olanzapine poInitial dose 5-10 mgOnce to twice a dayShort to long-term25 mg/dayB E
Increase the dose gradually by 5 mg at an interval of 7-14 days if the patient presents with psychosis.
Aripiprazole poInitial dose 2-5 mgOnce to twice a dayShort to long-term30 mg/dayB E
Increase the dose gradually at an interval of 3-14 days by 5-10 mg if the patient presents with psychosis.
Caution: SSRIs may cause agitation and an increased suicide risk during the first 2-4 weeks. TCAs can be fatal in overdose – conduct a suicide risk assessment at every follow-up visit and avoid them in patients with suicidal thoughts/attempt as much as possible. Avoid TCAs in children, the elderly and patients with heart disease, urinary retention, glaucoma and epilepsy. For depression with psychomotor agitation consider amitriptyline if no other contraindications; consider sertraline/fluoxetine for depression with psychomotor retardation.

TABLE 25: SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS IN THE MANAGEMENT OF MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDERS: Table 25: Special Considerations in the Management of Major Depressive Disorders (Special case, Intervention)
Special caseIntervention
If younger than 12 years• No antidepressants, provide counselling then refer
Pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers• Antidepressants should be avoided as far as possible and the refer
Depression with psychotic symptoms• Prescribe anti-depressants + anti-psychotics
BAD, depressive phase.• Prescribe mood stabilizer + anti-depressant + antipsychotic
If symptoms of mania emerge during treatment of depression• Immediately stop antidepressants and refer

Tables 26-27. Anxiety disorders: antidepressants (fluoxetine, sertraline) and short-term benzodiazepines in crisis (lorazepam, alprazolam, clonazepam) – doses, titration, maximum duration; cautions
MedicineDoseFrequencyDurationMax doseCodes
Table 26 - Antidepressants for anxiety disorders
Fluoxetine poInitial dose 10 mgOnce a dayShort to long-term60 mg/dayA E
Increase the dose gradually by 10 mg at an interval of 4-8 weeks if the patient still presents with anxiety symptoms.
Sertraline poInitial dose 25 mgBedtimeShort to long-term150 mg/dayA E
Increase the dose gradually by 25 mg at an interval of 7-14 days if the patient still presents with anxiety symptoms.
Table 27 - Benzodiazepines for short-term management (patient in crisis)
Lorazepam poInitial dose 1-2 mgOnce to three timesMaximum 2-4 weeks10 mg/dayB E
Increase the dose gradually by 0.5-2 mg at an interval of 3-7 days if the patient still presents with anxiety symptoms.
Alprazolam0.25-0.5 mgTwo to three timesMaximum 2-4 weeks4 mg/dayB E
Increase the dose gradually by 0.5 mg at an interval of 3-7 days if the patient still presents with anxiety symptoms.
Clonazepam poInitial dose 0.5-1 mgOnce to twice a dayMaximum 2-8 weeks4 mg/dayB E
Increase the dose gradually by 0.25-0.5 mg at an interval of 3-7 days if the patient still presents with anxiety symptoms.
Caution: benzodiazepines cause cognitive impairment (drowsiness) – warn patients not to drive, swim or operate machinery; the elderly are at risk of over-sedation, falls and hip fractures (consider low doses); dependence may occur after only a few weeks – do not prescribe continuously for long; do not prescribe to people at high risk of addiction (e.g. personality disorders, previous or current substance misuse).

Treatment duration: reduce the antipsychotic dose at each follow-up visit if mentally stable; maintain the lowest dose; consult a psychiatrist about discontinuing; if more than 3 episodes of psychosis, advise lifelong treatment. Caution: prescribe olanzapine and risperidone cautiously to the elderly and people with obesity, diabetes, hypertension or other cardiovascular conditions; one antipsychotic at a time, starting low and increasing gradually to an optimum dose for at least 4-6 weeks before considering it ineffective; treat side effects – do not provide an anticholinergic to every patient.

Guide for Interpreting PHQ-9 Scores (Score, Recommended Actions)

New: table with merged cells (as in the PDF)

Guide for Interpreting PHQ-9 Scores (Score, Recommended Actions)
ScoreRecommended Actions
0-4Normal range or full remission. The score suggests the patient may not need depression treatment.
5-9Minimal depressive symptoms. Support, educate
10-14Major depression, mild severity. Use clinical judgment about treatment, based on patient's duration of symptoms and functional impairment. Treat with antidepressant or psychotherapy.
15-19Major depression, moderate severity. Warrants treatment for depression, using antidepressant, psychotherapy or a combination of treatment.
20 or higherMajor depression, severe severity. Warrants treatment with antidepressant and psychotherapy, especially if not improved on monotherapy; follow frequently.
